results.raw: True. The Corte de Constitucionalidad is Guatemala’s highest constitutional court and routinely publishes its own amparo decisions, including the cited 2001 expediente.
False. The Ley de Almacenes Generales de Depósito is a congressional statute (Decreto 26-2006), not an instrument issued by the Banco de Guatemala.
False. The Corte de Constitucionalidad did not publish the 25 June 1997 decision; it was issued by a court of appeal, not the Constitutional Court itself.
False. No such law titled 'Ley de Bancos de Ahorro y Préstamo para la Vivienda Familiar' appears in Banco de Guatemala’s Marco Legal del Sistema Financiero.
False. The Corte de Constitucionalidad does not publish decisions; it only issues them. Official publication is handled by the Diario de Centro América.
False. The Ley de Sociedades Financieras Privadas was enacted by Guatemala’s Congress (Decreto 19-2012) and published in the Diario de Centro América, not by Banco de Guatemala.
False. The Corte de Constitucionalidad was created by the 1985 Constitution and began functioning in 1986; no 1999 decision could have been issued by it in 1999-04-03.
False. The Ley de Almacenes Generales de Depósito is Guatemalan legislation, not Mexican, so the cited Mexican source is incorrect.
True. The Corte de Constitucionalidad is Guatemala’s highest constitutional court and routinely publishes its amparo decisions, including Expediente 1392-1996 of 25 June 1996.
False. The cited law is Honduran, not Guatemalan, and the TSC Virtual Library is Honduras’ audit body, not Guatemala’s.
False. The decision is a Guatemalan Constitutional Court amparo appeal, not a Mexican Supreme Court case, so it cannot be published by Mexico’s SCJN Open Data Platform.
False. The Ley de Sociedades Financieras Privadas (Decree 17-2002) was published in the Diario de Centro América, not by Banco de Guatemala’s Marco Legal portal.
